description: Expose CLI commands for browse/list, manual add, edit, supersede, flag, and prune of findings, usable by both human operators and (later) the L3 agent.

requirements.description: Expose CLI commands covering the full findings lifecycle: (1) list/browse — paginated list with filter by status/brief/query; (2) add — manually add a finding with claim, citations, and confidence; (3) edit — update claim, confidence, or citations on an existing active finding; (4) supersede — mark a finding as superseded, require a replacement finding ID or reason, archive the original row; (5) flag — mark a finding as disputed with a reason string; (6) prune — remove findings matching a filter (dry-run mode required); destructive execution refuses without an explicit --force flag (no interactive confirmation prompt — prompts would conflict with programmatic agent invocation). All commands must be usable by both human operators via terminal and programmatically by the L3 agent as tool invocations.
requirements.title: Findings Management CLI Commands

validation.notes: `findings list` with --status=active returns only active findings
`findings list` with --status=superseded returns only superseded findings
`findings add` with valid claim and at least one citation creates a new finding with status=active
`findings add` missing required claim field returns a validation error with descriptive message

`findings edit` on a superseded finding returns an error (cannot edit archived findings) [guard implemented at the repository seam (every caller path — CLI, RPC, agent — inherits it): Edit rejects status=superseded with a validation error, preserving the archived row]
`findings supersede` transitions finding status from active to superseded and writes audit record with reason
`findings flag` transitions finding status from active to disputed and records the dispute reason
`findings prune --dry-run` outputs matched findings count without mutating the database

`findings prune` without --dry-run refuses to execute deletions unless the explicit --force flag is passed; the refusal names --force and issues no RPC [criterion amended 2026-06-10 from 'confirmation prompt': an interactive prompt conflicts with the sibling criterion that all commands run programmatically by the L3 agent without prompts — an explicit flag is the destructive gate that satisfies both]
L3 agent invokes `findings supersede` as a tool call and the finding status transitions correctly in the live database
CLI `findings list` executed against a database with mixed-status findings returns correctly filtered results
A human operator can fully manage the findings lifecycle (add, review, correct, supersede, flag) without direct database access
The L3 agent can invoke all findings management commands as tools without requiring human intervention for routine curation
